time_units: signed grant and contract declared execution timestamps are Unix milliseconds; monotonic performance fields are local process milliseconds
limitations: HTTP services share one Node process; local EVM node is a child process
command duration measures signed request to gateway response; client grant preparation is separate in auth_samples
policy order rotates over repeats; repeat=1 alone retains order and warmup effects
robot HTTP endpoint is an emulator; no physical robot action measured
controlled HTTP relay outage and response delay are injected, not real WAN observations
shortened TTLs test mechanisms and cannot establish minute-scale availability
5 planned commands plus one recovery command per run; no retries or request-load benchmark
no proactive half-life renewal: this benchmark tests pre-issued leases, not full stage4 scheduling
online authorization includes client grant issuance then online validation of that same bound grant
upload is explicitly triggered after recovery; setup/heartbeat/recovery probe costs are included in restoration-to-flush, not flush-only
same-process Date.now assumes trustworthy clock; crash and compromised bridge are outside this benchmark
local Ganache uses an ephemeral in-memory database; receipts are checked live and later replayed on a fresh node; no restart persistence claim
local Ganache development-node receipts do not establish public-chain finality or performance
few observations per run: request p95 is descriptive, not population inference
